 :: J U D G M E N T :

:
The petitioner has filed this claim petition against the respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest for the injuries sustained by him in a Road Traffic Accident.

2. The brief contents of the petition are as under:
On 05.07.2015 at about 4.00 pm., when the petitioner was riding the vehicle bearing reg.No.KA-42-Q-5663 slowly, cautiously by observing all traffic rules and regulations,
proceeding on the left side of the road, from Avalahalli towards Kanakapura main road.

When the petitioner reached at Tippasandra circle, Narayanapura 2 nd Block,
Bengaluru, at that time, a Car bearing reg.No.KA-35-M-6039 driven by its driver at high speed in a rash and negligent manner, all of a sudden came from Doddakallasandra and SCCH - 09 3 MVC No.7470/2018 dashed against the petitioner's vehicle.
Due to impact, the petitioner was thrown out from his vehicle and sustained severe injuries all over the body and his vehicle also damaged.

Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Sri Sai Ram Hospital,
Bengaluru wherein he took treatment as an inpatient.

The doctor revealed that petitioner sustained ring finger + middle finger proximal phalynx fracture of left hand, 3x3 cms CWW (+)ve over 4 th Web Space on Volar aspect and other injuries and the petitioner has spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards hospital charges, medicines,
conveyance, nourishing food and other incidental charges.
Prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy and working as loader and unloader, earning Rs.15,000/- per month.

The accident occurred due to sole rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Car bearing reg.No.KA- 35-M-6039 and Thalaghattapura police have registered a case against the driver of the said Car in their crime SCCH - 09 4 MVC No.7470/2018 No.305/2015 under Section 279, 337,
338 of IPC.
The respondent No.1 is the RC owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the car bearing reg.No.KA-35-M-6039.
Hence, both are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, on all these grounds, the petitioner prayed to allow this petition and award compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- under all heads together with interest and costs.
3. In response to the Court notice, the respondent No.2 has appeared before the court through its counsel and filed the written statement.
On the other hand, the respondent No.1 has not appeared before the court, remained absent and placed exparte.

4. The brief contentions of the written statement of respondent No.2 are as under:

sentences.text: The respondent contended that, petition is not maintainable in law, facts and circumstances of the case and petition is liable to be dismissed against this respondent.
Respondent denied the place, date and time of SCCH - 09 5 MVC No.7470/2018 alleged accident and also denied the income and avocation of the petitioner.

Respondent contended that, compensation claimed by the petitioner is exorbitant and further contended that, accident occurred only due to the sole negligence of the petitioner himself who ridden his two wheeler in rash and negligent manner, the driver of the car has not at all contributed in any negligence resulting in the alleged accident.
Further contended that the driver of the said alleged car was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the car as on the date of accident.
Further contended that, the car bearing reg.No.KA-35-M-6039 did not possessed FC at the time of alleged accident.
Further the respondent No.2 has contended that, the owner of the vehicle and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act.
Hence, on all these contentions, the respondent No.2 prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, my predecessor in office has framed the following issues :
 SCCH - 09 6 MVC No.7470/2018  ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that on 05.07.2015 at 4 pm., he was riding his motor cycle bearing No.KA- 02-Q-5663 cautiously by observing all the traffic rules and regulations on the left side of the road from Avalahalli towards Kanakapura Main road and when he reached at Thippasandra Circle,
Narayanapura 2nd Block, at that time, a Car bearing reg.No.KA-35/M-6039 driven by its driver came in high speed in a rash and negligent manner and hit the motorcycle of petitioner.
Due to the said accident he sustained grievous injuries as on date of alleged accident ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?
6. In order to prove the case, the petitioner examined himself as PW-1 and got marked the 16 documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.16.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has not adduced any oral or documentary evidences.

7. Heard arguments from petitioner and respondent and I have perused the records.
Petitioner has produced citations reported in :

3 2) (2018) 3 Supreme Court Cases 208 SCCH - 09 7 MVC No.7470/2018 3) 2023 ACJ 1245 and perused the same.

8. My findings to the above issues as follows:
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative  Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3: As per final order,
 for the following:
 R E A S O N S 9. ISSUE NO.1: It is the case of the petitioner that, on 05.07.2015 at about 4.00 pm., when he was riding the vehicle bearing reg.No.KA-42-Q-5663 slowly, cautiously by observing all traffic rules and regulations, proceeding on the left side of the road, from Avalahalli towards Kanakapura main road.

When he reached at Tippasandra circle, Narayanapura 2nd Block, Bengaluru, at that time, a Car bearing reg.No.KA-35-M-6039 driven by its driver at high speed in a rash and negligent manner, all of a sudden came from Doddakallasandra and dashed against the his vehicle.
Due to impact, he was thrown out from his vehicle and sustained severe injuries all over the body.
10. To prove the accident that occurred due to the sole negligence on the part of the rider of the offending Car SCCH - 09 8 MVC No.7470/2018 bearing reg.No.KA-35-M-6039.
The petitioner himself got examined as PW-1 and got marked the documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.16.

The Ex.P.1 is the statement, Ex.P.2 is the FIR, Ex.P.3 is the wound certificate, Ex.P.4 is the panchanama, Ex.P.5 is the IMV report, Ex.P.6 is the IMV report of respondent vehicle, Ex.P.7 is the sketch, Ex.P.8 is the inpatient bills, Ex.P.9 is the discharge summary, Ex.P.10 is the prescriptions, Ex.P.11 is the Aadhar card, Ex.P.12 is the notice U/s.133 of IMV Act, Ex.P.13&14 is the reply, Ex.P.15 is the 1st page of chargesheet and Ex.P.16 is the PAN Card.

11. On perusal of documents, police have investigated the matter and filed the charge sheet against the driver of the offending Car bearing reg.No.KA-35-M-6039 as per Ex.P.15 for the offence punishable under Sec.279, 338 of IPC and Section 187 of Motor Vehicles Act.
On perusal of said documents the owner and rider of the offending motor cycle have not disputed involvement of vehicles.
The respondent No.2 counsel suggested to the PW-1 as accident was occurred on his own negligence, but witness has denied SCCH - 09 9 MVC No.7470/2018 the said suggestion.
Further respondent No.2 suggested that the Car bearing reg.No.KA-35-M-6039 did not possessed FC at the time of alleged accident.
If it really true, respondent had to prove the same with documentary evidence, but respondent not made any effort produce the document to prove his defense.

Therefore, by considering the oral and documentary evidence on record and above discussion, I am of the opinion that, the accident was occurred on negligence of driver of the offending Car bearing reg.No.KA-35-M-6039.
The petitioner has produced the wound certificate as per Ex.P.3, that document discloses the petitioner has sustained grevious injury.
Hence, I answer the Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

sentences.text: Issue No.2:- In view of answering issue No.1 in the affirmative the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

To assess the compensation the Tribunal has to look into several facts like injuries,
pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment, medical and SCCH - 09 10 MVC No.7470/2018 attendant,
charges, conveyance, loss of income during treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc. let me discuss one by one:
a) TOWARDS INJURY, PAIN AND SUFFERING: The petitioner has contended that due to accident he sustained ring finger + middle finger proximal phalynx fracture of left hand, 3x3 cms CWW (+)ve over 4 th WEB space on volar aspect and other grievous injuries all over the body, treated conservatively with operation, after discharge he continued follow up treatment at Siddalingappa Memorial Hospital.

In order to prove injuries caused to him he has produced wound certificate/Ex.P3,
which reveals that petitioner has sustained simple as well as grievous injuries.

The petitioner has produced Ex.P.9- discharge summary of Sri Sairam Hospital wherein it discloses that petitioner took treatment in the hospital as an inpatient from 05.07.2015 to 06.07.2015 i.e., for 2 days.
The petitioner has not examined doctor to prove the disability.

As the petitioner sustained injury to the left hand and considering the avocation of the SCCH - 09 11 MVC No.7470/2018 petitioner it is just and proper to award the compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the head pain and sufferings.
b) TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has claimed compensation towards medical expenses.
The petitioner contended that he took treatment at hospital and produced Ex.P.8 - medical bills for Rs.76,438/- as per the memo calculation by the petitioner.
As there is no dispute about these medical bills, the Tribunal is of the view that petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.76,438/- is just and reasonable towards Medical Expenses.
c) TOWARDS FOOD, EXTRA NOURISHMENT, CONVEYANCE AND MEDICAL ATTENDANT CHARGES:
On perusal of Ex.P.9 - discharge summary it shows that the petitioner took treatment as inpatient at Sri Sairam Hospital from 05.07.2015 to 06.07.2015 i.e., for a period of 2 days.
During the time of treatment the petitioner also required good food and extra nourishment.

Considering the said fact the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of Rs.1,000/- per day for 2 days and also by including conveyance it is just SCCH - 09 12 MVC No.7470/2018 and reasonable to award Rs.4,000/- towards food extra nourishment, conveyance and medical attendant.
d) TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
The petitioner contended that he was doing loader and unloader in a Sand Lorry and earning Rs.15,000/- as a income.
In order to prove his income, he has not produced any documents to show that he was earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- p.m.
In the absence of positive documents regarding his occupation and income this Tribunal will consider notional income.
The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, fixed notional income of the year 2015 at Rs.9,000/- p.m.
Accordingly, the notional income of petitioner during the year 2015 treated as Rs.9,000/- p.m., Petitioner could not have carried out his avocation normally for at least one month.

By considering the facts and circumstances of the case this tribunal held that Shivakumar vs V.D. Vyasaraj on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84157182/
5 petitioner is entitled to Rs.9,000/- towards loss of income during laid up period.
e) Towards Future Earnings:

sentences.text: The petitioner has SCCH - 09 13 MVC No.7470/2018 contended that due to accident he was inpatient in the hospital and but petitioner has not examined doctor to show the disability.
In the absence of examining of doctor, it can assume that, petitioner may not sustained any disability.
Therefore, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head of loss of future earning capacity.
f) Towards Deprivation Of Future Amenities:

The petitioner has contended that, on account of the said injuries, he cannot lift or carry weight since there is no grip in his left hand, getting head ache and giddiness often, he cannot walk along distance, cannot stand long time and undergone deep mental shock, pain and sufferings, since the injuries caused are permanent in nature.
As per wound certificate, petitioner may sustained simple as well as grievous injuries.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of Rs.5,000/- is just and reasonable towards under the head of deprivation of future amenities.
g) FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
As the petitioner  SCCH - 09 14 MVC No.7470/2018 has not examined the doctor to prove any disability, therefore question of future medical expenses shall not arise.
Hence, petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head future medical expenses.

6 14.
Regarding Liability:

As already stated above the SCCH - 09 15 MVC No.7470/2018 petitioner has proved that the accident in question was caused by the driver of the Car bearing reg.No.KA-35-M-6039 with rash and negligent act.

It is the contention of the respondent No.2 that,
as on the date of accident driver of offending car was not holding valid and effective driving licence.
But respondent No.2 failed to prove its contention.
Moreover, the driver of the offending Car was holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
The respondent No.2 has admitted issuance of policy in favour of respondent No.1 in respect said Car bearing reg.No.KA-35-M- 6039.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the R.C.owner and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

However,
the respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending vehicle is primarily liable to pay the compensation with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.
15. ISSUE NO.3:

In view of my finding on issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following;
 SCCH - 09 16 MVC No.7470/2018  O R D E R
The petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,24,438/- with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

However, in view of the policy, the respondent No.2/insurance company is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner and directed to deposit the compensation amount in this tribunal within one month from the date of this order.
After deposit of compensation amount, the entire amount with accrued interest shall be released on proper identification through e-payment.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
